'''Tyler Smith''' (born November 2, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He has previously played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].

==Early life and high school career==
Smith was born in [[New Orleans, Louisiana]] and relocated with his family to [[Houston, Texas]] after they were was displaced by [[Hurricane Katrina]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Crain|title=Walking Mismatch: G League Ignite's Tyler Smith Blends Fluidity with Size|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/g-league-ignite-tyler-smith-fluidity-size-story-background-nba-draft|website=[[SI.com]]|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023}}</ref> Smith attended [[George Bush High School]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Young|title=Bush's Tyler Smith leaving school to sign with Overtime Elite|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/highschool/article/Bush-Tyler-Smith-Bryce-Griggs-Overtime-Elite-OTE-16405358.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=August 23, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2023}}</ref>

Smith was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, ranked 8th by [[ESPN]], 15th by [[247Sports|247]] and 18th by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] before leaving school for OTE according to major recruiting services.<ref name="OTEliteZucker">{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Zucker|title=5-Star PF Tyler Smith Skips College, Signs '7-Figure' Overtime Elite Contract|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10010869-5-star-pf-tyler-smith-skips-college-signs-7-figure-overtime-elite-contract|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=August 22, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2023}}</ref> He had scholarship offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], among others.<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Young|title=How Bryce Griggs, Tyler Smith are doing at Overtime Elite|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/hs-sports/article/Bryce-Griggs-Tyler-Smith-OTE-Overtime-Elite-pro-17674056.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=December 26, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Smith opted not to pursue a collegiate career and signed a two-year contract with [[Overtime Elite]] (OTE), a new professional league based in Atlanta with players between ages 16 and 20, on August 22, 2021.<ref name="OTEliteZucker" /><ref>{{cite web|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|title=Tyler Smith, No. 8 basketball prospect in 2023 class, signs with Overtime Elite|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/32069127/tyler-smith-no-8-basketball-prospect-2023-class-signs-elite|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=August 22, 2021|access-date=November 14, 2023}}</ref> In his second season, he played for team Cold Hearts and was named second team All-OTE after averaging 15.7 points, eight rebounds, 1.9 steals, and 1.3 blocks per game.<ref name="NBGLIgnTipton">{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Tipton|title=Overtime Elite's Tyler Smith signs with G-League Ignite|url=https://www.on3.com/news/overtime-elite-tyler-smith-signs-with-g-league-ignite/|website=On3.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=November 16, 2023}}</ref>

Smith signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]] on June 30, 2023.<ref name="NBGLIgnTipton" /><ref>{{cite press release|title=Tyler Smith & Izan Almansa Sign With Ignite|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/tyler-smith-izan-almansa-sign-with-ignite|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=November 20, 2023|archive-date=July 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230702214536/https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/tyler-smith-izan-almansa-sign-with-ignite|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Smith was selected with the 33rd overall pick by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Young|title=NBA draft: Bucks pick former Houston high school standout Tyler Smith|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/rockets/article/nba-draft-tyler-smith-bucks-houston-19542803.php|work=[[Houston Chronicle]]|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 27, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Milwaukee Bucks Select Tyler Smith With 33rd Pick In 2024 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-select-tyler-smith-with-33rd-pick-in-2024-nba-draft |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> and on July 5, he signed with them.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign AJ Johnson and Tyler Smith|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-aj-johnson-and-tyler-smith|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}}</ref> Smith made his NBA debut on October 23, in a 124–109 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks at Philadelphia 76ers Box Score, October 23, 2024.|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230PHI.html|website=BasketballRef|access-date=November 1, 2024}}</ref> On December 17, Smith won his first NBA honours playing the final minutes in the [[2024 NBA Cup]] final in a 97-81 win against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|title= In-Season Tournament Final: Milwaukee Bucks at Oklahoma City Thunder Box Score, December 17, 2024.|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202412170OKC.html|website=BasketballRef|access-date=December 17, 2024}}</ref> Throughout his rookie season, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Wisconsin Herd Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Wisconsin-Herd/50/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 18, 2024}}</ref> Smith made 23 appearances for Milwaukee during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 2.9 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 0.2 assists.

Smith was waived by Milwaukee on October 20, 2025, after losing a training camp roster battle to [[Amir Coffey]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Tyler Smith: Waived by Bucks | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-10-20 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tyler-smith-waived-by-bucks/ | access-date=2025-12-05}}</ref>

On October 25, 2025, Smith was selected second overall by the [[Osceola Magic]] in the [[2025 NBA G League draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=South Bay Lakers Select NBA Champion Dillon Jones with First Pick in 2025 NBA G League Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-select-nba-champion-dillon-jones-with-first-pick-in-2025-nba-g-league-draft|access-date=October 25, 2025|website=gleague.nba.com|language=en}}</ref>

On December 3, 2025, Smith signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rockets Add Tyler Smith, Part with Kevon Harris|url=https://www.si.com/nba/rockets/onsi/news/rockets-add-tyler-smith-part-with-kevon-harris|access-date=December 6, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> Smith was waived on January 3, 2026 without playing in a game for the Rockets.<ref>{{cite press release|title= Rockets Sign Tristen Newton |url= https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-tristen-newton |website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2023|access-date=January 4, 2026}}</ref>

On March 1, 2026, Smith signed a two-way contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mavericks sign two new players, waive rookie guard|url=https://basketnews.com/news-242176-mavs-two-way-deals-tyler-smith-john-poulakidas.html|access-date=March 7, 2026|website=basketnews.com|language=en}}</ref> On July 20, Smith was waived by the Mavericks after making 12 appearances for the team, having averaged 4.7 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 0.4 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mavericks waive two-way forward Tyler Smith following multiple roster moves|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/article/mavericks-waive-two-way-forward-tyler-smith-22353060.php|access-date=July 20, 2026|website=[[Dallas Morning News]]|language=en}}</ref>
